_what: Bias audit of the released profiles, computed from the paper's own 500-profile three-annotator human evaluation (1,500 judgements). Each judgement is the mean of the five rated axes. MEASURED 2026-09-03 by src/make_fairness_macros.py's source.
_why: ECIR 2027's resource-paper CfP requires authors to address fairness, including potential biases in data, annotations or tool behaviour, and mitigation.

by_popularity._method: items split into equal thirds by ML-20M rating count
by_popularity._reading: flat; the resource does not degrade on cold items, which is where a content feature is most needed

by_genre._method: primary_genre as recorded on the annotation sheet, genres with n>=15 judgements
by_genre._reading: systematic and small; comedy is the weakest genre

unquantified: profiles are English-only, generated by an English-centric model over a Western-skewed catalogue
three annotators, not demographically sampled; blinded to model identity but with a fixed column order rather than a randomised one
the ten mood axes are researcher-chosen bipolar scales, not validated against users
